Start group-kill test timeout once its child is ready (TODO 253) (#282)

TODO 253 records 1 run of tools/test-skill-release-date-client.py
that errored with FileNotFoundError for sleeper.pid in
test_a_child_that_does_not_end_is_killed_with_its_group, and 3 reruns
that passed; a rerun that passes does not clear a failure. That is the
TODO's record, not a check of this change.

The 1 second timeout started before the stub child had forked its
sleeper and written sleeper.pid, so a slow start let the group kill
land before the pid file existed. Host load is the inferred cause of
the slow start; a 2 second delay before the pid write reproduces the
error.

The sleeper, its pid file and the probe of its pid with os.kill are
removed. The stub child now forks 1 member into its group and then
writes 1 byte to a FIFO, alive, and the client's first wait starts
only once the test reads that byte, polled for at most 60 seconds, as
in the capped-child test beside it; the poll is new to this test. The
test asserts the client's reason first, then that the byte was read
when the poll ended, that the client asked its first wait for exactly
its 1 second timeout, that the real wait lasted at least that long,
and that the client's run, from its start to its return, less the
poll, ended within 15 seconds; main bounded the whole run by 15
seconds.

End of file on alive within 10 seconds after the client returns shows
that the client killed the whole group, not only the leader: it comes
only once every process holding the write end has ended. Its time is a
clock read taken after the read that sees it, and a time past that
deadline counts as not seen. Each stub process otherwise ends by
itself 90 seconds after it enters its wait for the release, and so
more than 90 seconds after the test's start. The check takes no end of
file seen later than 85 seconds from that start, the 60 second poll,
the 15 second run and the 10 second check, plus the poll's last step,
and end of file must come before 90 seconds, so the group's own end is
never taken for the kill.

The test sends no signal. Each stub process waits for end of file on
a second FIFO, lifeline, whose only write end the test holds, and
ignores SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP. The check's finally clause closes
lifeline and reaps a child the client left unreaped, and the kernel
closes lifeline when the test process ends in any other way. The stub
reads lifeline once before it forks, a read the planned design did not
have. On Linux, select reports nothing for a FIFO reader opened with
no writer, so a stub that starts after the release would otherwise
wait out its 90 seconds; that read returns end of file, so with the
read it exits at once. A stub process past that read ends at once on
the release; one not yet there ends when it reaches it, after the rest
of its start-up, which the test does not bound.

The stub's source is a constant. The stub first reads its own end with
float from a file, own_end, that the check writes, so no value of
own_end adds code to the stub; a text that float does not take raises
before the stub opens either FIFO, and the check fails.

New tests run the check against a client that kills only the leader,
one that sends SIGTERM to the group, and a client whose group kill
raises KeyboardInterrupt, and assert that each fails or passes the
interrupt through and that the group ends within 5 seconds after it.
Another runs it against a stub whose own end falls inside the check
and asserts that it fails at the own-end assertion, another asserts
that a stub started after the release exits at once, and another
asserts that an end of file seen after its deadline is not taken. A
tripwire test asserts that the stub makes its pinned calls in order
and that no signal-sending name appears in the check, its helpers or
the stub, so a direct os.kill there fails it. The group-kill test
asserts nothing about the client's reap; its docstring names the 2
tests that do.

Reduced coverage, which landing this change accepts: the test has no
allowlist of the check's callees, no pin of the calls that start a
process with their arguments, no type test of check and own_end, no
check that they are not rebound, no check of the stub's calls for
example values of own_end, and no test that a caller's value runs no
code of its own.

Residual: the tripwire's name scan misses every route to a signal
other than a signal-sending name in the functions it reads, and such
an edit passes the tripwire unless it also changes the stub's calls,
which the pin rejects. Passes of the name scan include, in the check,
getattr(os, "kill") with a literal name, getattr with a computed
name, os.__dict__["kill"], vars(os)["kill"] and a shell kill through
os.system, and also the witness a caller passes, a module global a
caller rebinds, a decorator's body and the client itself. A value of
check or own_end with methods of its own runs them in the test.

A stub process that the release finds before its first read of
lifeline outlives the release by the rest of its start-up. While the
test process is alive but neither closes lifeline nor ends, as when
it is stopped, each stub process lives its start-up plus 90 seconds.
A client whose real wait gives up early by less than the time the
gate's 2 clock reads and the call add passes; the call's share
includes the wait's overrun past its own deadline, which the code
does not bound, so the host sets the margin.

A process that inherits the write end of lifeline and outlives the
test would keep the stub alive up to its own end; only a fork without
exec in the test process could do that. A stub process that closed
its copy of alive before it ended would hide from the check; only an
altered stub could do that. A process that SIGKILL cannot end keeps
alive open and fails the check. A leader that has not ended within
the 5 second reap grace of the finally clause, or one left when the
test process ends without unwinding, stays unreaped until Python's
own collection of finished children or the process that adopts it
reaps it. The stub ignores SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP; a signal it
does not ignore whose default action ends a process, such as SIGKILL
or SIGUSR1, still ends it early. A correct client still fails if the
child is not ready within 60 seconds. The design needs FIFOs, select
on them and the Linux behaviour that a FIFO reader opened while a
writer exists sees end of file when the last writer closes. The
expected outcomes are for Linux; for other platforms and for the
Python 3.9 floor they are not established.

Unchanged from main: the 1 second timeout, the reason string, the
real wait, kill and reap, and a 10 second window for the group to end
after the client returns. With a 2 second delay before the pid write,
main's test fails. A client that kills only the group leader, one
that never kills, one whose first wait asks for half its timeout and
one whose real wait gives up at half its timeout each fail the new
test.

The client's run_extractor catches Exception broadly and leaves its
child's group running when KeyboardInterrupt passes through it; that
is left for a later item.

  the Pull request text gate.
